title: EU AI Act Compliance Readiness: A Technical Assessment of Mid-Tier European Startups

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: a compliance readiness assessment is descriptive and useful for identifying gaps, but does not directly improve safety. Market concentration effects are speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: checking startup documentation against EU AI Act requirements demands understanding of the legal text and the ability to operationalize compliance criteria.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: surveying 20+ startups is very broad for 30 hours. Even checking public documentation for that many companies would be superficial.

novelty.reasoning: EU AI Act compliance readiness is heavily studied. The EU published an official AI Act Compliance Checker at artificialintelligenceact.eu. Silicon Canals reported that over 60% of small/mid-sized tech companies are not adequately prepared (February 2025). The Cloud Security Alliance published a research note on the enterprise readiness gap for the high-risk deadline. Multiple compliance guides exist (SecurePrivacy, LegalNodes, DataGuard, SIG). However, most existing work focuses on self-reported survey data or generic compliance guidance rather than a technical documentation audit of specific startups. The proposed hands-on assessment of 20+ startups' public documentation against specific EU AI Act requirements would add granularity, but the broad finding (most startups are unprepared) is already established and the scope of 20+ companies is very ambitious.

evidence: EU AI Act Compliance Checker. artificialintelligenceact.eu.
